key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden or over minutes. LOCATION: RETROSTERNAL (behind breastbone), left-sided chest, or epigastric. RADIATES to left arm, jaw, neck, back, or both arms. DURATION: Continuous for >10-20 minutes, does NOT resolve with rest. CHARACTER: CRUSHING, pressure, squeezing, heaviness, "elephant on chest". NOT sharp or stabbing typically. AGGRAVATING: None (unprovoked, can occur at rest). RELIEVING: NOT relieved by position change, antacids, or nitroglycerin (if severe). TIMING: Persistent, progressive worsening. SEVERITY: 7-10/10, most severe pain patient has ever felt. KEY POSITIVES: Diaphoresis (sweating), nausea, vomiting, dyspnea (shortness of breath), sense of impending doom, pallor, weakness. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT sharp, NOT positional, NOT pleuritic (worse with breathing).

red_flags: Radiation to left arm or jaw
